rewrites.summary: Enforcement is the live risk for a trans visitor here: the 2024 attempted femicide (femicidio frustrado) of trans woman Kenia Chacón in Punta Arenas drew four years' internación parcial against the five years' internación total the prosecution sought — a judicial precedent of under-penalisation for gender-motivated violence against trans women that places Magallanes below the national average (−0.06 vs 0.72) — while the regional director of SernamEG (the national women and gender-equality service) has publicly criticised the sentence as not reflecting the gravity of the attack and announced an appeal, a genuine institutional counter-signal that prevents a deeper deduction. Absolute case volume is low (0.96 % of the national case total), but the reduced-sentence precedent is a severity signal for a visitor. No source addresses border screening, document practice, or marriage/partner-travel consequences for trans visitors here.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Adjacent context: versus national 0.72 this region sits at −0.06; the neighbouring Tarapacá (0.64) is 0.02 lower, because its Iquique court annulment voids the femicide protection for trans women in that jurisdiction entirely, whereas this region applied the femicide framework but under-sentenced. The April 2026 appeal announced by the regional women and gender-equality service is litigation in flux — no outcome is recorded.
rewrites.localsOnly:
Resident-facing case facts: the 2024 attempted femicide concerned a resident, and the victim's mother publicly denounced the devaluation of the attack on the basis of her daughter's gender identity; the regional director of SernamEG (the national women and gender-equality service) criticised the sentence as not reflecting the gravity of the attack.

The 2024 national dataset (the annual Movilh human-rights report) records this region at 0.96 % of the national case total, among the regions with the largest percentage increases (+100 % year-on-year).
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: No source addresses border-screening or document-practice for trans visitors, and no marriage- or partner-travel-specific rule or incident is recorded — the visitor assessment rests on the judicial finding and the case-share signal alone. The April 2026 appeal has no recorded outcome. The case-share figures (0.96 % of the national total; +100 % year-on-year) rest on the annual Movilh report dataset, which no region-specific source independently covers (rule 5).
